thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — elevated error rate detected for /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1. 5xx spike started ~14:05 UTC, current 5m 5xx% = 18%. Paging oncall.

maria: i'm oncall and looking. i'm seeing p95 latency jump and a bunch of 503/504s in the gateway logs. will collect traces. @kevin can you grab quota-service metrics?

kevin: pulling metrics now. there's also a correlated spike of 429s from rate-limiter around the same time. quota-service saw a config change at 14:02 — new tenant burst/window rollback was supposed to be staged but appears rolled to prod accidentally.

john: checking config audit — i can see the deploy: person=eng-deploy, commit=ab4f9c, change=default_tenant.window_ms: 60000 -> 10000. that reduces smoothing and causes tighter enforcement. when combined with a cache-miss fanout we're getting request amplification -> 429s -> gateway back-pressure -> 503s.

elaine: support: several customers reported timeouts (ticket #12345, #12346). customer-james reports 6 failed requests in a row. marking impacted customers for notifications.

kevin: logs snippet from quota-service:
```
2026-03-15T14:06:11Z WARN quota-check tenant=alpha key=default quota=100 window_ms=10000 current=95 -> REJECT 429
2026-03-15T14:06:12Z ERROR gateway-proxy upstream=runtime-01 status=502 msg="upstream timeout"
2026-03-15T14:06:13Z INFO cache miss model-prefix=kvcache key=abc123 fanout=6
```

maria: good catch. immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback quota config to previous window (safe), 2) temporarily raise per-tenant burst caps, 3) enable circuit-breaker on gateway for heavy fanouts, 4) route traffic to lower-concurrency model variant to reduce load. i'm going to attempt #1 first (rollback config).

john: i can apply rollback. command i'll run:
```bash
# apply previous quota window
kubectl -n infra apply -f /manifests/quota-configs/quota-default-window-60000.yaml
# restart quota-service so config reloads quickly
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/quota-service
```

maria: go for it. i'll notify customers after we confirm recovery.

deploy-bot: Started rollout restart for deployment/quota-service in namespace infra (rollout id: r-20260315-1409).

kevin: seeing config back to window_ms=60000 in config-store at 14:18 UTC. applying traffic metrics watch...

maria: confirmed, 5xx% trending down from 18% -> 4% over last 3 minutes. 429s also dropping.

elaine: opened status update to affected customers: "We've identified a quota config issue causing elevated errors; we've rolled back the change and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause." sending now.

kevin: post-rollback metrics (14:20 -> 14:28): p50 latency stable, p95 back to baseline 120ms, 5xx% <1% except for a few in-flight failures.

maria: mitigation successful. next steps: 1) write a postmortem, 2) add guardrails to deploy pipeline to block direct quota window changes without canary, 3) add a temporary circuit-breaker to gateway for model fanouts, 4) create a runbook step for rapid rollback. john, can you open GH issue and link infra PR?

john: created issue #789: "misapplied quota-window caused 5xx cascade" and PR #790 for a deploy pipeline gate. adding checklist and runbook edits.

kevin: adding short-term telemetry alert tweak: create a composite that alerts on simultaneous spike of 429+5xx for same route to avoid missing config-induced cascades.

maria: handing incident to eng-sre for full postmortem + followups. lena will take post-incident lead for next 48h.

lena: acked. i'll coordinate the RCA and customer follow-ups. thanks all. :thumbsup: 

maria: incident resolved and monitoring clear for 20m. final status: SEV2, duration ~00:16 from page to mitigation start, ~00:56 to full recovery. root cause: accidental release of tighter quota window combined with cache miss fanout causing cascading 429 -> gateway 5xx. actions: rollback, deploy pipeline gate, runbook updates, telemetry alerting. closing thread and will attach timeline + logs to the incident ticket.

deploy-bot: Incident note added to ticket INC-20260315-42.
